intents: Troubleshoot why the SSH-like TCP service on server port 22 does not respond from client.
The service is running on server, and an alternate TCP service on port 2222 is already reachable through fw.
The failure is caused by firewall filtering on fw, not by addressing or routing.
Add the minimal nftables forward-path rules required to allow TCP port 22 from client to server and its return traffic.
Keep TCP port 2222 working and keep unrelated ports such as TCP 23 blocked.
Do not flush/reset firewall state and do not modify management connectivity on eth0.

fw: nft add rule inet filter forward iifname "eth1" oifname "eth2" tcp dport 22 ct state new,established accept
nft add rule inet filter forward iifname "eth2" oifname "eth1" tcp sport 22 ct state established accept

ground_truth_reasoning: Addressing and routing are valid because the alternate service on port 2222 traverses the firewall. The missing piece is a forward-path ACL for TCP/22. The minimal repair is to permit new/established client-to-server SSH traffic on fw eth1 to eth2 and the established return flow from server to client, leaving the existing default-deny posture and other blocked ports intact.

baseline_invariants.name: client management interface is still up
fw management interface is still up
server management interface is still up

testcases.name: TCP port 22 responds after firewall repair
Firewall audit shows allow rule for SSH
